title: A Walk Around Ann Arbor & U-M

places.name: Start: S Main & E William
places.note: Start here, downtown. Head north on Main Street.

places.name: Main Street (turn at Kingsley)
places.note: Main Street is the more grown-up side of Ann Arbor: restaurants, bars and shops. Walk north until Kingsley St, then turn right (east).

places.name: Zingerman's Deli
places.note: A classic. If College GameDay is ever in Ann Arbor, you'll see a shot of Zingerman's. A great deli, and a good place to stop for a meal if you're hungry.

places.name: East Liberty Street
places.note: Head back south on Division St, then east on Liberty. E Liberty is the more student-feeling stretch of downtown. Turn left (north) on State St when you reach it.

places.name: Burton Memorial Tower
places.note: From State St, go right (east) on E Washington to Ingalls Mall. This is the bell tower.

places.name: Michigan League (optional)
places.note: Optional. Worth poking your head in if it's open.

places.name: Hill Auditorium
places.note: Cross the street after the tower. Peek in if it's open.

places.name: The Diag
places.note: Cross N University Ave and keep going down Ingalls Mall to the Diag, the heart of central campus. Look for the brass block "M" in the middle: students avoid stepping on it. Legend says if you step on it, you'll fail your first exam.

places.name: Angell Hall & the Fishbowl
places.note: Go into Angell Hall and see the Fishbowl computer lab. For lack of a better term, it's the heart of LSA (the College of Literature, Science, and the Arts).

places.name: Shapiro Library (and Hatcher)
places.note: If seeing the library is on the list: Shapiro is the undergrad library where students actually hang out. It's connected to Hatcher, the grand graduate library.

places.name: Engineering Arch
places.note: Leave the Diag through the arch under West Hall (southeast corner). It lets you out at S University & East University.

places.name: East Quad
places.note: Walk south on East University. East Quad has a weird residential program (the Residential College). I'd recommend Will NOT do it.

places.name: Ross School of Business
places.note: Right (west) on Hill St, then right (north) on Tappan. The new Ross building, which didn't exist when I was there.

places.name: Law Quad & Law Library Reading Room
places.note: Go diagonally across the street to the front of the Law Quad. Go look at the Law Library Reading Room if someone will let you in (access may be limited). Tell Will he can pretend he's Harry Potter by studying there.

places.name: Michigan Union
places.note: Exit the Law Quad onto State St. The Union has some food options.

places.name: The Cube
places.note: Officially "Endover," in Regents Plaza. For some unknown reason, a Michigan landmark. It spins if you push it.

places.name: Rally House
places.note: Walk north on State St: the university on your right, shops on your left, and more shops past where campus ends. Rally House is where to buy some swag if Will is into it.

places.name: Back downtown via Liberty
places.note: Head west on Liberty back to Main Street. The start is one block south.

places.name: Zingerman's Deli
places.note: The classic (also stop 3).

places.name: Cottage Inn Pizza
places.note: Classic undergrad pizza.

places.name: Pizza House
places.note: Great undergrad food, a block off the East University leg.

places.name: Frita Batidos
places.note: A newer place that's good. Cuban-inspired street food, downtown.

places.name: Michigan Union
places.note: Some food options inside (also stop 15).

places.name: Palmer Field
places.note: The main freshman dorms are all around this field. This is where Will might live freshman year.

places.name: Stockwell Hall
places.note: Freshman dorm on Observatory St.

places.name: Mosher-Jordan ("MoJo")
places.note: Freshman dorm on Observatory St.

places.name: Alice Lloyd Hall
places.note: Freshman dorm on Observatory St. Couzens and Markley are nearby too.

places.name: Nichols Arboretum (the Arb)
places.note: If it's a really nice day and you have time. It's right next to the Hill dorms, so it's an easy add-on to that detour: from Observatory St, walk east to the end of Washington Heights and you're at the edge of the Arb. The trails head down to the Huron River.

places.name: North Campus (engineering)
places.note: If Will is considering engineering, you need to go up to North Campus. It's a drive or a U-M bus from Central Campus, not part of the walk. Worth seeing: Lurie Tower (this pin), the Duderstadt Center next door, and the Wave Field.
